items.abstract: <jats:p>Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual data for 17 G20 countries over 2000–2021, this study examines the effects of social welfare (SCWF), economic policy uncertainty (ECPX), trade openness (TROP), life expectancy (LIEX), natural resource rents (NARN), and tourism (TRSM) on ecological footprints (ECFP). Employing a Pooled Mean Group–Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) model, the analysis captures both short-run dynamics and long-run equilibrium relationships while accounting for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity across countries. The findings reveal that natural resource rents and social welfare expansion significantly increase ecological footprints, indicating that resource-intensive development and consumption-oriented welfare systems can undermine environmental sustainability. Life expectancy and economic policy uncertainty are negatively associated with ecological footprints. These estimates do not establish causal effects or demonstrate the influence of environmental regulation, which is not measured in the model. Trade openness exerts mixed effects, increasing environmental pressure in the short run but promoting ecological sustainability in the long run, whereas tourism consistently intensifies ecological degradation. These findings highlight the complex trade-offs between economic prosperity, social progress, and environmental protection in G20 economies. From an SDG perspective, the results provide important implications for achieving SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). The study advocates integrated policy frameworks that promote sustainable resource management, environmentally responsible tourism, and balanced welfare strategies to support long-term ecological resilience and sustainable development.</jats:p>
title: From welfare to the environment: social policy, natural resources, and ecological sustainability in G20 economies

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is marked by pronounced urban heterogeneity, so that a uniform account of its carbon emission drivers is unlikely to hold. Using panel data for 11 cities from 2015 to 2023, this study applies the Generalized Divisia Index Method to decompose eight drivers of emission change and to classify the cities by their factor contribution structures. Economic growth (G) and output carbon intensity (CI) are the largest positive and negative contributors in ten of the eleven cities (mean G = +19.18%, mean CI = −9.94%), the exception being Macao. An exploratory Ward clustering of the four most variable factors, cross-validated against k-means, distinguishes four types of driving structure—carbon-intensity suppression, economic-scale driven, energy-scale expansion, and a specialized service-structure type (Macao); an innovation index combining research and development (R&amp;D) intensity and patent density varies independently of these types. Decoupling is likewise uneven, ranging from strong decoupling in three cities (Foshan, Zhongshan and Hong Kong; Tapio elasticity t = −0.152 to −0.437) to weak decoupling in six (0.133 ≤ t ≤ 0.462) and expansive coupling in Huizhou and Macao. Per-capita emissions and energy-structure carbon intensity show marked dispersion. These findings inform a three-tiered policy discussion—differentiated measures, collaborative governance, and data support—for coordinated low-carbon governance in urban agglomerations.</jats:p>
title: Decomposition of carbon emission drivers and urban typology in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: implications for regional environmental management

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Groundwater recharge is traditionally understood to be primarily controlled by precipitation and other climatic processes. However, intensive anthropogenic water management and urbanization may weaken this relationship in megacities. This study investigates hydrological decoupling at the municipal scale in Beijing, China, and quantifies the relative contributions of anthropogenic and climatic drivers to groundwater dynamics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyzed 19 years of multisource hydroclimatic data using nonparametric trend analyses, antecedent-window correlation analyses, and hierarchical multiple regression. Spatial analyses were conducted to examine the potential effects of impervious surfaces and managed vegetation on natural groundwater recharge. Future drought risks and groundwater trends were also assessed under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 climate scenarios for 2024–2100.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Annual precipitation showed no statistically significant correlation with groundwater depth (Spearman’s ρ = 0.04, p = 0.624), and no significant delayed associations were identified across antecedent climatic windows of 1–12 months. Hierarchical regression attributed 60.0% of the variance in groundwater depth to anthropogenic drivers, represented by total water supply, compared with 35.6% attributed to natural climatic forcing. Spatial analyses further indicated that dense impervious surfaces and managed vegetation may constrain natural recharge and weaken the influence of meteorological variability on groundwater dynamics. Both future climate scenarios indicated substantial drought risk, while historical evidence suggested that groundwater trajectories would remain strongly influenced by active water management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate that anthropogenic water management can become a dominant control on urban groundwater dynamics, potentially outweighing the influence of climatic variability. This hydrological decoupling challenges conventional assumptions about precipitation-driven groundwater responses and highlights the importance of integrating water governance, urban land-surface characteristics, and climate adaptation into groundwater management strategies for heavily urbanized basins.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Hydrological decoupling of groundwater from natural climatic forcing in a heavily managed megacity

                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Agricultural-waste-derived activated carbons offer a sustainable alternative to conventional adsorbents; however, most studies rely on single biomass precursors and evaluate adsorption using only one model pollutant.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, a hybrid activated carbon (HAC) derived from banana peel and olive pomace was developed and evaluated for the removal of four structurally distinct dyes: methylene blue (MB), methyl orange (MO), crystal violet (CV), and Eriochrome Black T (EBT). The effects of adsorbent dosage, pH, and contact time were investigated, followed by adsorption isotherm, kinetic, and regeneration analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An adsorbent dosage of 12 g/L and pH 2 provided the most favorable adsorption conditions. The hybrid activated carbon was found to have a high removal efficiency of 97.71% for MB, 98.41% for MO, 98.70% for CV, and 98.95% for EBT, respectively, under the optimized conditions to remove different dyes with different chemical structures. The equilibrium data were generally better described by the Langmuir model, while the adsorption kinetics showed stronger agreement with the pseudo-second-order model. HAC exhibited maximum adsorption capacities of 130.34, 99.70, 112.42, and 114.52 mg/g for MO, MB, CV, and EBT, respectively, with hybridization enhancing the adsorption capacities toward MO and EBT compared with the individual activated carbons. Regeneration experiments showed that HAC retained adsorption functionality after ten cycles, although removal efficiencies decreased to approximately 42%–56%.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results in this study validate the potential of olive pomace and banana peel-based hybrid activated carbon as a waste derived, reusable material for the removal of dyes from contaminated wastewater, thereby valorizing agricultural waste and promoting sustainable resource utilization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Sustainable hybrid activated carbon from banana peel and olive pomace for efficient removal of structurally diverse dyes

<jats:p>
                    Most of the user-interface of toilets is associated with
                    <jats:italic>in-situ</jats:italic>
                    , decentralised wastewater treatment systems. Specifically, on-site sanitation systems (OSS) and decentralised wastewater treatment systems (DEWATS) are mainly used to treat toilet blackwater (faeces, urine, and flush water). Though ideal, malodour generated within these systems can hinder their adoption, especially where sanitation infrastructure is limited. Perceived desirability and social acceptability of toilets are negatively influenced by malodour and is a major contributor to its non-use and disuse. Obnoxious odours emanate largely from bacterial activity under anaerobic conditions, through the production of volatile organic sulphur compounds, nitrogenous compounds, and volatile fatty acids. Conventional odour-abatement strategies are plagued by substantial operational inputs and generation of secondary waste streams. Against this backdrop, bacteriophages are being investigated as a precision biological option, due to their host-specificity, and ability to self-amplify. This review examines bacteriophage-based strategies alongside established approaches for managing odour-causing microorganisms, with emphasis on emission points, biochemical processes, toxicity, translational bottlenecks, and research priorities.
                  </jats:p>
title: From ‘yuck’ to ‘ahhh’: a focused review on the bacteriophage-based strategy for malodour mitigation to improve the aspirational quotient of toilets

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Rio Grande, an important river that borders the USA and Mexico is recharged with untreated and treated wastewaters from binational sources and therefore is known to contain potentially toxic elements (PTEs) like As, Cd, Co, Cr, Pb, and Sb. These elements are nonbiodegradable and can accumulate in soil and crops when contaminated surface water is used for irrigation. This study was designed to assess the contamination levels of these elements in water, soil, and crops sampled from three farms (onion, cilantro, and Swiss Chard in Hidalgo Co., TX) and use the data to perform pollution assessment (bioaccumulation factor - BAF, enrichment factor - EF, and metal pollution index - MPI) and health hazard assessment (health index-HI, estimated daily intake–EDI, and cancer risk - CR). Matrixes were digested and analyzed using ICP-OES. The mean PTE concentrations in water (0.73–81.74 ug/L) were all within acceptable levels for irrigation water. Although the mean concentration of PTEs (mg/kg) in soil Cd (0.19), Co (5.04), Cr (10.04), and Pb (18.36) were within acceptable limits, all three had above normal levels of Sb (11.64–18.62) with elevated As levels detected in the onion and Swiss chard fields (7.35 and 8.20, respectively). The mean dry weight of As and Cr in onion, cilantro, and Swiss chard tissues were either above normal or excessive (As 2.90 mg/kg – 5.85 mg/kg; Cr 0.71 mg/kg – 15.79 mg/kg), but all crop tissues had normal or below normal levels of Sb (mean 9.50 mg/kg). Swiss chard tissues also had elevated levels of Cd, Co, and Pb (0.25 mg/kg, 7.04 mg/kg, and 19.11 mg/kg, respectively). Health risk assessment showed that the EDI of all PTEs studied in the crops were within the US FDA daily acceptable intake limits; the HI for cilantro was safe for cilantro, but high for onion and Swiss chard. CR assessment for cilantro was acceptable across all the metals studied, whereas CR for onion and Swiss chard were above the threshold and were considered unacceptable. These results indicate that chronic consumption of crops that bioaccumulate PTEs can present systemic toxicological risks within the water-energy-food nexus.</jats:p>
title: Assessment of trace metals in irrigation water, soil, and vegetables along the US-Mexico border and their health risks

items.abstract: <jats:p>The synergy of industrial transformation and ecological security is an important pair in the regional high-quality development. Previous studies of the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration have mainly examined industrial development, ecological carrying capacity, low-carbon transition, or environmental resilience separately, leaving the coordinated evolution of industrial structure optimization and urban ecological resilience insufficiently understood. This gap is particularly relevant for late-developing coastal urban agglomerations, where rapid industrial restructuring occurs alongside increasing ecological pressures. To address this issue, taking the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration as the study area, an evaluation system for industrial structure optimization and urban ecological resilience was constructed, and the coupling coordination between the two systems was examined from 2012 to 2022. The contribution of this study lies in integrating industrial structure optimization (ISO) and urban ecological resilience (UER) within a unified analytical framework and simultaneously examining their temporal evolution, spatial differentiation, subsystem-lagging characteristics, and interacting driving factors. The findings extend the empirical understanding of industrial–ecological coordination in late-developing coastal urban agglomerations and provide a quantitative basis for differentiated sustainability governance. Results indicate that the industrial structure optimization and the urban ecological resilience had steadily improved over the study period, however, there remained large inter-city variation. The average coupling coordination degree rose from 0.338 in 2012 to 0.432 in 2022, which reflects the changing trend of mild disorder-to-near-order but overall systems still not into the coordinated development stages. At the spatial level, the coordination pattern was featured with a remarkable core, higher values in northern regions and differentiated performance among coastal port cities. Nanning booth performed as a leader city and FangchengGang better Chongzuo always weak. The results of the geographical detector show that development of digital economyhas a dominant explanatory power on gross regional environmental quality, followed by science–technology input, economic development, transport accessibility and environmental regulation. The results of interaction detection indicate that the synergistic effect of digital economy and science-technology input has the strongest explanatory power. These findings identify the major factors and interaction patterns associated with spatial differences in industrial–ecological coordination and provide quantitative evidence for differentiated governance in late-developing coastal urban agglomerations.</jats:p>
title: Urban ecological resilience and industrial structure optimization coupling coordination in the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration

Constraining dispatch to the nine documented pumping stations reduces the realizable volume to 55.08 MIGD (61% of the aggregate optimum) when each field feeds a single station, quantifying the cost of the full-connectivity assumption; the binding constraint stays on the distribution side in every case. <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Groundwater is the primary dependable freshwater source in the arid coastal catchments of western Saudi Arabia, where natural recharge is limited and occurs mainly through episodic rainfall and flash‐flood infiltration along wadi systems. This study assesses groundwater potential in the Wadi Marwani basin (≈2,347 km
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      ), a major tributary of the Khulais system southeast of Rabigh, by integrating multi‐source remote sensing, GIS, and aeromagnetic data.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lithology was mapped from Sentinel‐2 imagery using support vector machine (SVM) classification, while structural fabrics were constrained using Sentinel‐1C SAR lineaments and aeromagnetic structural analysis. Terrain attributes (e.g., elevation, slope, drainage and flow indices, topographic wetness, and ruggedness) derived from a 30 m digital elevation model (DEM), together with NDVI, soil moisture, rainfall, and 10 m land‐cover data, characterized the surface conditions that control infiltration and storage. Aeromagnetic data were reduced to the pole, upward continued, and enhanced using the modified Elliott function (MEF) filter and Center for Exploration Targeting (CET) grid analysis. Source Parameter Imaging (SPI) was then applied to estimate relative depth to magnetic basement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Surface and magnetic lineaments consistently define a dominant N–S to NNW–SSE trend with subsidiary NW–SE and NE–SW sets that remain coherent at depth, reflecting reactivated Pan–African structures. A magnetically subdued, elongate basement depression along the central wadi axis, widening westwards, coincides with high lineament density and thick Quaternary alluvium, indicating favorable conditions for groundwater accumulation. The integrated groundwater potential map divides the basin into five classes; comparison with existing wells yields an AUC of 0.789, indicating acceptable to good predictive skill.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The most promising zones lie along the central wadi corridor and the western alluvial plain. The integrated workflow is readily transferable to other basement‐controlled arid catchments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Combined aeromagnetic, GIS, and remote sensing evaluation of flash-flood susceptibility and groundwater potential in an arid environment: Wadi Marwani, Western Saudi Arabia

items.abstract: <jats:p>Global climate governance increasingly relies on understanding the spatial mismatch between carbon emissions and ecosystem carbon sequestration capacity. As a critical regulating ecosystem service, carbon sequestration service flows exert substantial interregional spillover effects through spatial ecological interactions. However, existing research has largely focused on static supply–demand evaluations at regional scales, while the spatial flow processes and driving mechanisms of carbon sequestration service flows across cities remain insufficiently explored. This study quantified the supply, demand, and flows of carbon sequestration service flows across 333 prefecture-level administrative units in China from 2010 to 2024 using breakpoint–field strength models and spatial flow analysis. Furthermore, the XGBoost-SHAP model was adopted to detect the nonlinear driving mechanisms behind carbon sequestration service flows. The results showed that China’s carbon sequestration service flows presented a potential west-to-east linkage pattern, indicating a pronounced spatial mismatch between carbon sequestration supply areas and carbon emission demand areas. High-supply regions were predominantly distributed in western and northern China, whereas demand regions were concentrated in eastern coastal urban agglomerations. The total volume of carbon sequestration service flows first rose and then declined over the study period, while the radiation distance and spatial interaction of service flows continuously increased. The potential spatial linkage of carbon sequestration service flows were identified: Inner Mongolia-Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yunnan–Guizhou–Pearl River Delta, and Northeast China/Sichuan-Xinjiang-eastern coastal urban agglomerations. XGBoost-SHAP analysis showed that PRE, DEM, TEMP, and GDP exhibited prominent main effects. PRE and TEMP had the strongest interaction, with DEM-TEMP and DEM-GDP showing relatively strong interactions compared with other variable pairs. The findings revealed the potential spatial linkage pattern of carbon sequestration service flows and offered scientific support for interregional ecological compensation and spatially coordinated carbon governance in China.</jats:p>
title: Spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of urban carbon sequestration service flows in China

items.abstract: <jats:p>Sustainable spatial planning is critical for reconciling rapid urbanization with low-carbon transitions, yet the spatial differentiation of transport carbon emissions (TCE) and its moderating factors remain insufficiently integrated into planning frameworks. This study examines how built environment factors influence TCE under the 5Ds framework in Guangzhou, China, using mobile phone signaling data, multi-source spatial data, and the GeoDetector model. We reveal three key findings. First, TCE exhibits a polycentric agglomeration pattern, reflecting finger-like urban expansion. Second, development intensity (FAR) is the strongest explanatory factor (q = 0.309), with the FAR–employment accessibility interaction showing the strongest synergistic effect (q = 0.323), validated as genuine nonlinear enhancement, indicating that density regulation and jobs-housing coordination must be planned jointly. Third, building height and housing price stratifications reveal monotonic gradient effects—FAR’s explanatory power increases from low-rise to high-rise areas and from low-price to high-price zones—demonstrating that uniform policies may exacerbate spatial inequities. Land surface temperature shows an inverted U-shaped moderating effect, highlighting the need for climate-adaptive planning. These findings support a differentiated, context-sensitive planning framework that integrates density regulation, jobs-housing coordination, and climate-adaptive design, moving beyond the conventional assumption that uniform-built environment interventions yield uniform carbon outcomes.</jats:p>
title: Spatial differentiation of transport carbon emissions under the 5Ds framework: implications for sustainable spatial planning in Guangzhou, China
